units.unitName: Introduction to information theory: Uncertainty, Information and Entropy, Information measures for continuous random variables, source coding theorem. Discrete Memoryless channels, Mutual information, Conditional entropy.
Source coding schemes for data compaction: Prefix code, Huffman code, Shannon-Fano code & Lempel-Ziv coding; channel capacity. Channel coding theorem. Shannon limit.
Linear Block Code: Introduction to error correcting codes, coding & decoding of linear block code, minimum distance consideration, conversion of non-systematic form of matrices into systematic form.

Cyclic Code: Code Algebra, basic properties of Galois fields (GF), polynomial operations over Galois fields, generating cyclic code by generating polynomial, parity check polynomial. Encoder & decoder for cyclic codes.

Convolutional Code: Convolutional encoders of different rates, code tree, trellis and state diagram. Maximum likelihood decoding of convolutional code: Viterbi Algorithm, free distance of a convolutional code.

Compiler, Translator, Interpreter definition, phases of compiler, bootstrapping, review of finite automata, lexical analyzer, input, recognition of tokens, LEX and lexical analyzer generator, error handling.

Review of CFG, ambiguity of grammars, introduction to parsing. Top-down parsing, LL grammars and parsers, recursive descent parsing, predictive parsers, bottom-up parsing, shift-reduce parsing, LR parsers, SLR, CLR and LALR parsing tables, operator precedence parsing, YACC and error handling.

Syntax directed definitions; syntax trees, S-attributed and L-attributed definitions, top-down translation. Postfix notation, DAG, three-address code, TAC for control structures, triples and quadruples, Boolean expressions and control structures.
Storage organization; storage allocation strategies, activation records, local/non-local names, parameter passing, symbol table organization and data structures.

Basic blocks and control-flow graphs; DAG representation, optimization, loop optimization, global data-flow analysis, loop-invariant computation, peephole optimization, code-generator design and code generation from DAG.
Introduction: Objective, scope and outcome of the course.

Introduction and history of operating systems: structure and operations; processes and files. IPC, mutual exclusion, semaphores, wait/signal, process scheduling, critical sections, threads and multithreading.
Memory management: contiguous allocation, virtual memory, paging, page-table structure, demand paging, page replacement, thrashing, segmentation and case study.

Deadlock: shared resources, resource allocation and scheduling, resource graphs, detection, avoidance and prevention. Device management: devices, drivers, device handling, disk scheduling algorithms and policies.
File management: file concept, types and structures, directory structure, case studies, access methods and matrices, file security and user authentication.
UNIX and Linux operating systems as case studies; real-time operating systems and mobile OS case studies.
Basics of Computer Graphics: basics/applications, display devices, random and raster scan systems, graphics input devices, graphics software and standards.

Graphics primitives: points, lines, circles, ellipses, scan conversion, scan-line polygon filling, inside-outside test, boundary/flood fill, character generation, line/area/character attributes, aliasing and introduction to anti-aliasing.

2D graphics: translation, rotation, scaling, matrix representation, homogeneous coordinates, composite transformations, reflection, shearing, viewing pipeline, window-to-viewport transformation and point/line/polygon clipping including Cohen-Sutherland, Liang-Barsky and NLN.

3D graphics: display methods, polygon surfaces, meshes, curved surfaces, quadric surfaces, splines, cubic spline interpolation, Bezier and B-spline curves/surfaces, 3D transformations, viewing pipeline, parallel and perspective projection.
Illumination and colour models: light sources, illumination models, halftone/dithering, chromaticity, RGB, YIQ, CMY, HSV and HLS colour models, colour selection.

Animations and realism: animation sequences, raster animation, key frames, motion specification, morphing, tweening, Koch/C/dragon/space-filling curves, fractals, grammar-based models, turtle graphics and ray tracing.
Background: review of algorithms, complexity/order notations and calculating complexity. Divide and Conquer: Binary Search, Merge Sort, Quick Sort and Strassen's matrix multiplication.
Greedy Method: Knapsack, Job Sequencing, Optimal Merge Patterns and Minimal Spanning Trees. Dynamic Programming: Matrix Chain Multiplication, Longest Common Subsequence and 0/1 Knapsack.
Branch and Bound: Traveling Salesman Problem and lower-bound theory. Backtracking and N-Queens. Pattern Matching: Naive, Rabin-Karp, KMP and Boyer-Moore.

Assignment Problems: Assignment and Quadratic Assignment. Randomized Algorithms: Las Vegas, Monte Carlo, randomized Min-Cut and 2-SAT. Multicommodity flow, flow-shop scheduling and network-capacity assignment.
Problem Classes: P, NP-Hard and NP-Complete, decision problems, Cook's theorem, Satisfiability and Vertex Cover; approximation algorithms for Vertex Cover and Set Cover.

Wireless channels: large-scale path loss, free-space/two-ray models, link budget, small-scale fading, multipath parameters, time dispersion, coherence bandwidth/time, Doppler spread, delay spread, flat/frequency-selective fading, fast/slow fading.

Cellular Architecture: FDMA, TDMA, CDMA, capacity calculations, cellular concept, frequency reuse, channel assignment, handoff, interference, capacity, trunking, grade of service, coverage and capacity improvement.
Digital Signaling for Fading Channels: wireless link structure, Offset-QPSK, pi/4-DQPSK, MSK, GMSK, error performance, OFDM, cyclic prefix, windowing and PAPR.
Multipath Mitigation: equalization, adaptive/linear/non-linear equalization, zero forcing, LMS, diversity, micro/macrodiversity, combining, error probability and RAKE receiver.
Multiple Antenna Techniques: MIMO, spatial multiplexing, system model, precoding, beamforming, transmitter/receiver diversity, channel-state information, capacity in fading and non-fading channels.
Introduction: Objective, scope and outcome of the course.
Historical evolution, interactive system design, usability, HCI and software engineering, GUI design/aesthetics and prototyping.
Model-based design/evaluation: models, GOMS, KLM, CMN-GOMS, Fitts' law, Hick-Hyman's law and case studies.
Guidelines: Shneiderman's eight golden rules, Norman's seven principles/model, Nielsen's ten heuristics, heuristic evaluation, contextual inquiry and cognitive walkthrough.
Empirical research methods: motivation, issues, research questions, experiment design, data analysis and one-way ANOVA.
Task modelling: HTA, engineering task models, CTT, dialog formalism, FSM, state charts and Petri Nets; computer animation types/relevance, Model Human Processor, OOP and object-oriented UI modelling.
Introduction: Objective, scope and outcome of the course.
Introduction: Basics of biology.

Sequences: problem statement, edit distance, substitution matrices, HMMs/pairwise HMMs, global/local alignment, spliced alignment, space-efficient alignment, multiple alignment, database-searching tools, sequence by hybridization and profile HMMs.
Structures: protein structure alignment and protein structure prediction.
Phylogenetic trees: large and small parsimony problems, probabilistic approaches and grammar-based approaches.
Miscellaneous topics: pathways and networks, microarrays and biomedical images.
Introduction: Objective, scope and outcome of the course.
Digital image representation, sampling and quantization, steps in image processing, image acquisition and color image representation.

Intensity transforms, histogram processing, spatial filtering, Fourier transforms/properties, frequency-domain filters, color models, pseudo-colouring, color transforms and basics of wavelet transforms.
Image degradation/restoration, noise models/filters, degradation function, inverse filtering and homomorphic filtering.
Coding redundancy, interpixel redundancy, psychovisual redundancy, Huffman coding, arithmetic coding, lossy compression and JPEG.
Point/line/edge detection, thresholding, edge/boundary linking, Hough transforms, region-based segmentation, boundary representation and descriptors.
Introduction: Objective, scope and outcome of the course.
Supervised learning: types/applications, Linear Regression, Naive Bayes, Decision Tree, KNN, Logistic Regression, SVM and Random Forest.
Unsupervised learning: k-means, hierarchical/probabilistic clustering, association rules, Apriori, FP-growth and Gaussian Mixture Model.
Statistical learning theory, PCA, SVD, feature selection/ranking/subset selection, filter/wrapper/embedded methods, evaluation and model selection.
Semi-supervised and reinforcement learning: MDP, Bellman equations, Monte Carlo policy evaluation, policy/value iteration, Q-Learning, SARSA and model-based RL.
Recommender systems, collaborative/content-based filtering, ANN, perceptron, multilayer networks, backpropagation and introduction to deep learning.
Introduction: Objective, scope and outcome of the course.
Security attacks, services/mechanisms, substitution/transposition ciphers, cryptanalysis, stream and block ciphers.
Block-cipher structure, DES, strength/design principles, AES structure/transforms/key expansion, multiple encryption, Triple DES, ECB, CBC, CFB, OFB and Counter modes.
Public-key cryptosystems: requirements/cryptanalysis, RSA, Rabin, ElGamal and Elliptic Curve Cryptosystem.
Hash functions, requirements/security, CBC-based hashes, SHA, MACs, digital signatures, ElGamal/Schnorr signatures and NIST DSA.
Key management/distribution, public-key distribution, X.509, PKI, remote authentication, Kerberos, web security, SSL, TLS, HTTPS and SSH.
Introduction: Objective, scope and outcome of the course.

Data representation, complements, fixed/floating point, register transfer and micro-operations, RTL, bus/memory transfers, arithmetic/logic/shift micro-operations, ALU, basic computer organization, instruction codes/registers, timing/control, instruction cycle, memory-reference instructions, I/O/interrupts and basic-computer design.

Basic computer programming: machine/assembly language, assembler, loops, arithmetic/logic operations, subroutines, I/O programming; microprogrammed control, control memory, address sequencing and control-unit design.

CPU: general-register and stack organization, instruction format, addressing modes, data transfer/manipulation, program control, RISC, pipelining/vector processing, Flynn taxonomy, parallel processing, arithmetic/instruction/RISC pipelines, vector/array processors.

Computer arithmetic: addition/subtraction, Booth multiplication, division, floating-point/decimal arithmetic; I/O organization/interface, asynchronous transfer, modes, priority interrupt, DMA, IOP, CPU-IOP communication and serial communication.

Memory hierarchy, main/auxiliary/associative/cache/virtual memory; multiprocessors, interconnection, arbitration, inter-processor communication/synchronization, cache coherence and shared-memory multiprocessors.
Introduction: Objective, scope and outcome of the course.
AI and intelligent agents; approaches to AI; problem solving by search; BFS, DFS, iterative deepening, bidirectional search, hill climbing, heuristic/greedy/A*/AO* search and constraint satisfaction.
Game playing: Minimax, alpha-beta pruning, jug problem, chess problem and tiles problem.
Knowledge/reasoning: knowledge bases, propositional logic, first-order logic, situation calculus, theorem proving, planning, partial-order planning, uncertainty, probabilities and Bayesian networks.
Learning: forms of learning, supervised learning, decision trees, SVM, unsupervised learning, market basket analysis and neural networks.
Introduction to NLP, issues in NLP, expert systems and robotics.
Introduction: Objective, scope and outcome of the course.
Cloud Computing: enabling technology, history, vision, characteristics/components, challenges/risks, migration, ethics, business impact/economics, future, networking support and ubiquitous cloud/IoT.

Cloud architecture: reference model, layers/types, service models, data-centre design/interconnection, compute/storage clouds, cloud programming, parallel/distributed paradigms, MapReduce, Hadoop and Google App Engine.
Virtualization: definition/benefits, implementation levels, tools/mechanisms, VMware/KVM/Xen, CPU/memory/I/O, virtual clusters/resources, server/desktop/network/data-centre virtualization.

Cloud security: fundamentals, services, design principles, policy, challenges/architecture, legal issues, data security, business continuity/disaster recovery, risk mitigation, threats, SLA and trust management.
Industry platforms: AWS, Google App Engine, Microsoft Azure, Aneka, private/public cloud integration; applications in protein prediction, data analysis, satellite image processing and CRM.
Introduction: Objective, scope and outcome of the course.

Features/nodes, distributed computation paradigms/models, centralized/network/distributed OS, cooperative autonomous systems, design issues, goals/transparency/services/architecture/DCE; time/state, events, clocks, precedence and recording state.

Concurrent processes/programming, processes/threads, graph models, client/server, time services, synchronization, resource servers, IPC, message passing, request/reply/transaction communication, naming/directory services, RPC and RMI.

Distributed scheduling, performance model, static scheduling, dynamic load sharing/balancing, distributed process implementation; distributed file systems, transparency, design/implementation, transaction/concurrency control, replication and case studies.

Distributed shared memory, NUMA, consistency models, multiprocessor caches, DSM implementation; causality, snapshots, failures, mutual exclusion, election, distributed deadlock and termination detection.
Distributed agreement, faults/failure/recovery, Byzantine faults/agreement, consensus impossibility/randomized agreement; replicated data, atomic multicast, update propagation and CORBA.
Introduction: Objective, scope and outcome of the course.
History/evolution of SDN, control/data-plane separation, IETF forces, active networking, advantages/disadvantages and OpenFlow.
Network virtualization, applications/frameworks, VMware, Mininet; control plane and controllers including Floodlight and OpenDaylight.
Control-plane customization: switching/firewall using SDN; software/hardware data planes and programmable network hardware.
Programming SDNs: northbound API, languages/tools, SDN composition, NFV concepts/implementation/applications.
Data-centre networks: packet/optical/wireless architectures, topologies and SDN use cases in data centres, IXPs, backbone, home networks and traffic engineering; programming assignments.
Introduction: Objective, scope and outcome of the course.
E-Commerce: commerce, activities, benefits, goals, components, functions, process, types, Internet/Web role, technologies, systems, prerequisites, scope and e-business models.
E-Commerce activities, modes, matrix of types, resources, providers/vendors, manpower, opportunity development, business case and website design/development.
Internet backbone: early Internet, networking categories, characteristics, Internet services/elements, URLs, IP, shopping cart, cookies, website communication and strategic capabilities.
ISP, WWW and portals, homepage/metadata, portal advantages, EIP; online publishing, strategies/approaches and online advertising.

XML goals, HTML vs XML, business importance, applications, document structure, XHTML/X-Secure; data warehousing, data marts/ODS; e-marketing, web presence, site adhesion, website maintenance, metrics and online marketing.
Point-to-point transformation: thresholding, histogram evaluation and histogram equalization.
Geometric transformations: rotation, scaling, translation and two-dimensional Fourier transform.
Linear filtering using convolution and highly selective filters.
Ideal frequency-domain filters, nonlinear filtering using convolutional masks and edge detection.
Morphological operations: erosion, dilation, opening, closing, open-close and close-open.
Implement FIND-S using training samples read from CSV.
Implement Candidate-Elimination using CSV training examples.
Implement decision-tree ID3 and classify a new sample.
Build an Artificial Neural Network using backpropagation and test it.
Implement Naive Bayes and compute classifier accuracy.
Use Naive Bayes for document classification; calculate accuracy, precision and recall.
Construct a Bayesian network for heart-disease diagnosis.
Apply EM and k-means clustering on the same CSV dataset and compare quality.
Implement KNN on the Iris dataset and print correct/wrong predictions.
Implement non-parametric Locally Weighted Regression and draw graphs.
Demonstrate basic Python data types.
Compute distance between two points; create add.py taking two command-line arguments and printing their sum.
Check even number; print decimal equivalents of 1/2 through 1/10 using a for loop.
Demonstrate list/tuple; loop over a sequence; create a while-loop countdown.
Find sum of primes below two million; sum even-valued Fibonacci terms not exceeding four million.
Count string character frequencies using a dictionary; use split/join and trace a birthday with a dictionary.
Count character frequency in a file and investigate whether it is a Python program, C program or text file.
Print each file line in reverse; compute number of characters, words and lines.
Implement nearly-equal strings and one-line GCD/LCM functions.
Implement Merge Sort, Selection Sort and Insertion Sort.
Study Android Studio/installation and create Hello World.
Understand Activity and Intent; create a login module checking username/password.
Design a simple GUI application with Activity/Intent, e.g. calculator.
Develop an application using RSS Feed.
Draw basic graphical primitives on screen.
Create an Android app using SQLite database.
Develop a native application using GPS location information.
Implement an application that writes data to the SD card.
Design a gaming application.
Handle images and videos according to size.
